gap: No result ChatGPT got sorts the extenders by how their makers' labels play out on an M3 Air with the lid open: a one-panel Alt Mode screen works in full with no software, while a two-panel extender lights its second panel only through a driver. Macworld's Trio 3 Pro review says a standard M3 can run both panels without the software, which contradicts Apple's own M3 page.
standout_why: Three pages already state the general rule. Apple 117373 (cited) says the second display goes dark when the lid opens. Plugable's Apple-silicon page (result 10, not cited) says macOS mirrors through MST hubs and that a DisplayLink dock adds displays. DeskExpander (result 7) says to choose a single-panel monitor or add DisplayLink with the lid open. DisplayLink's setup page (cited) covers the app and the screen-recording permission. None of them names an extender or ties a maker's 'plug & play', 'driver-free' or 'M1/M2/M3 compatible' wording to the M3 Air's lid-open limit. The new part is that product-level mapping, and the Macworld statement that conflicts with Apple.
decides: If the shopper wants one added screen, buy a single-panel USB-C Alt Mode screen. The Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS is our row, and Mobile Pixels says it extends over a single cable. If they want two added screens with the lid open, only a driver path lights both: the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro with Mobile Pixels' display software, or a DisplayLink adapter. The shopper should not rely on Macworld's line that a standard M3 needs no software. The FOPO dual models we list as 'driver-free' (S1, S7, S10, S11) should not be the pick for three screens on an M3 Air until FOPO's own pages confirm how each panel is fed. Apple's limit implies that a driver-free second panel stays dark or mirrors with the lid open, but that is an inference, not something FOPO states.

findings.label: MacBook Air M3 external displays, lid closed vs lid open
findings.value: Two external displays with the lid closed (primary up to 6K 60 Hz, secondary up to 5K 60 Hz); if the lid is opened with both connected, the secondary display goes dark or disconnects
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's page gives no lid-open count in words; it only says the second display goes dark. The page does not mention DisplayLink, MST or drivers. It says a display that can only mirror through a hub should be connected directly to the Mac.

findings.label: Base M3 display count, and how macOS handles MST and DisplayLink
findings.value: Base M3: one external display with the lid open, two with it closed. Lid-closed mode needs macOS Sonoma 14.3 or later on MacBook Air. macOS doesn't support MST for extended displays, so an MST dock, hub or adapter mirrors. A DisplayLink dock can add up to four displays and needs the DisplayLink Manager app plus screen-recording permission.
findings.source_title: MacBook Docks and Monitor Limits, M1 to M6 ~ Plugable Technologies
findings.note: Plugable's words: 'macOS doesn't support MST (Multi-Stream Transport) for extended displays' and 'If you daisy-chain monitors or use an MST dock, hub or adapter, macOS mirrors the displays instead of extending them.' This means a two-panel extender that splits one USB-C video signal without a driver cannot extend both panels on a Mac. This page was in ChatGPT's results but was not cited.

findings.label: DeskExpander's advice for the M3 Air
findings.value: 'drives one external display with the lid open and two with the lid closed'; 'With the lid open, choose a single-panel monitor, or add DisplayLink for the second panel.'
findings.source_title: MacBook Air M3: external monitor guide | DeskExpander
findings.note: This was in ChatGPT's results (rank 7) but not cited. It names no extender models.

findings.label: Drawbacks of the driver path (DisplayLink / InstantView)
findings.value: 60 Hz refresh-rate caps and potential latency
findings.source_title: How do I get my two screens to show different things? (Mobile Pixels blog, Apr 20, 2026)
findings.note: Mobile Pixels' words: 'these solutions have drawbacks including 60Hz refresh rate caps and potential latency'. The same post says 'the M3 has to have its lid closed to enable a second display.'

findings.label: Video path (maker's blog)
findings.value: Extends over a single USB-C or USB-A cable; Mobile Pixels says the OS recognises it as a fully independent display
findings.source_title: Why Are My Two Monitors Showing the Same Display? (Mobile Pixels blog, Apr 23, 2026)
findings.note: The blog says 'Duex DS' and does not spell out 'Duex Max DS'. Our record for the Duex Max DS says: one USB-C cable with DisplayPort Alt Mode and no driver, or USB-C plus mini HDMI. The USB-A route would need a driver; the blog does not say so. On an M3 Air with the lid open this is the one native external display, so it works in full. The same post says the M3 supports two external displays natively only with the lid closed.

findings.label: Two panels on a base-M-chip MacBook: Macworld's wording vs Apple's limit
findings.value: Two included USB-C cables. Per the manual Macworld quotes, no driver is needed when the laptop has two DP-enabled USB-C ports. Base M1/M2 need Mobile Pixels' free software (Macworld: 'rather like DisplayLink'). Macworld also writes that 'A MacBook with anything as or more powerful than a standard M1/M2/M3 processor' can drive both screens without the download.
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: This is the normalising footnote. Simon Jary tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro, not an M3 Air. Apple 117373 says an M3 Air's second external display goes dark with the lid open, and Plugable says base M3 drives one with the lid open. So on an M3 Air with the lid open, the Trio's second panel needs Mobile Pixels' software even though the Air has two video-capable USB-C ports. Fit ranges also differ: Macworld says 13- to 16-inch MacBooks, while our record carries Mobile Pixels' range as 15–16 inches. I did not re-open the maker page today (see unsourced).

findings.label: Store price, Mobile Pixels US
findings.note: Read with storecheck search on mobilepixels.us. This matches our record's store price for 2026-11-21.
